claim: CBC provides substantial incremental predictive value for iron-deficiency triage.
evidence: Tier-2 ΔAUROC approximately +0.29 in both observed and matched iron analyses; all six model families support positive mean T2 gain.
permitted_language: substantial incremental value; consistent across model families
avoid_language: CBC causes better outcomes; universally optimal

claim: CBC adds little incremental discrimination for vitamin-D screening.
evidence: Mean Tier-2 minus Tier-1 AUROC approximately -0.0015; 0/6 model families support positive mean Tier-2 gain.
permitted_language: little or no incremental predictive value

claim: Iron Tier 2 provides greater confirmatory-testing efficiency than Tier 1.
evidence: At the 90% training-sensitivity target, Tier 2 avoids materially more ferritin testing than Tier 1.

claim: Temporal instability cannot be characterized by elapsed time alone.
evidence: Vitamin D shows clearer temporal attenuation; iron patterns differ after eligibility matching and across measured distribution shifts.
permitted_language: consistent with multiple sources of temporal shift
avoid_language: we proved the cause of model drift

claim: Ferritin eligibility changes create substantial population-distribution discontinuity.
evidence: Stage 04 matching reduced I-to-J mean |SMD|, PSI, and JSD substantially.

claim: Eligibility matching does not fully restore iron predictive transport.
evidence: Observed-versus-matched Stage-07 performance differences were small or negative in multiple bridge analyses.
permitted_language: residual predictive instability remains after matching

claim: OOF probability recalibration substantially improves probability reliability.
evidence: Sigmoid recalibration improved Brier score in all study/tier experiment groups and ECE in essentially all.

claim: Survey weighting does not overturn the principal Tier-1/Tier-2 discrimination conclusion.
evidence: Weighted AUROC changes are modest and retain the vitamin-D T1≈T2 and iron T2≫T1 ordering.

claim: The iron Tier-2 result is robust to exclusion of ages 18–19.
evidence: Age 20–59 evaluation changes iron Tier-2 AUROC only minimally without retraining.
permitted_language: robust to the 20–59 structural sensitivity analysis
avoid_language: education missingness has no effect whatsoever

evidence: Stage 08 evaluates sex, race/ethnicity, age and poverty groups subject to minimum support rules.
permitted_language: subgroup transportability was examined; performance heterogeneity was quantified
avoid_language: the model is fair; no disparities exist
